_meta.title: Orthographic origin markers
_meta.description: Letter patterns whose presence in a word signals its language of origin, used to disambiguate origin-sensitive graphemes from the SPELLING ALONE (never from a word lookup). Conditioning a grapheme's sound on co-occurring marker graphemes is a pure-grapheme rule: you detect Greek-ness from 'ph'/'ps'/'y', not from knowing the word.
_meta.source_notes: Conditioning sound on the identity of neighboring graphemes: Kessler & Treiman (2001, 2003). Multi-sound-phonogram / origin framing for 'ch': Orton-Gillingham tradition; Eide (2018) reports the Greek/French/English three-way for 'ch'.
_meta.status: seed — expand markers and origin-sensitive graphemes

greek.notes: A medial 'y' acting as a vowel (gym, myth, system) is a strong Greek signal; so are the onset clusters chr-/sch- (chrome, scheme) and word-initial ps-/rh-/mn-/pn-.

sounds.condition: word also contains a Greek marker (ph, ps, chr, sch, medial-y)
word also contains a French marker (-ine, -que, -et, ou)

residue.note: Words with NO distinguishing marker cannot be resolved from letters alone and belong to the memorize-list.
